title: I Took the Credit-Union Night-Drop Camera to the Teller Who Denied It

parts.text: I dropped an envelope at 8:02 p.m. and the next morning the teller said it never happened. The night-drop sticker she placed said: CAMERA ON 24/7. KEEP YOUR RECEIPT STUB. I was forty-four, small-business member, holding the stub with the time punch. Teller Rita said, "Stubs jam. Cameras loop." I pointed at her sticker. She shrugged. "Loops aren't evidence." I photographed the stub, the sticker, and the empty batch list. Then I asked a supervisor to pull the 8:02 still. At 9:11 the supervisor asked why Rita's drawer was on a denied-drop ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The supervisor can see the 8:02 still of my hand on the drop Rita denied.

social.video_title: She said the night drop never happened — Part 1/2
social.description: Time-punch stub, a 24/7 sticker, and a loop excuse. I asked for the still. Would you have redeposited cash?

parts.text: Rita called it a training miss until the still showed her walking past the chime. I printed the ticket, the sticker, and the frame. The envelope was in the overflow bin she had not opened. Rita told the vault the sticker was always about optics. Optics is a word tellers use when a chime has a face. Drop policy now has a second line: LOOPS ARE EVIDENCE. I keep stubs. Rita opens overflow. The chute finally counts.

social.video_title: Loops are evidence at the night drop — Part 2/2
social.description: Denied-drop ticket, overflow bin, and a second line on the sticker. Was a jam ever a walk-past?
